originalReview.notes: Exact725x1159published Qualla1911advertisement inspected. Printed PalaceHotelCompany/NewPalaceHotel/MarketandNewMontgomery text and whole rebuilt1909corner photograph bind surviving eight-storey block, repetitive rectangular openings,top arched row,strong cornice and rounded corners. Exact nativeSHA1matches primaryPD-retouched-user/Centpacrr original upload declaration, same dimensions and publisher/1911publication identity. Retouch released by original uploader. Low-resolution dated photo does not establish modern sign, rooftop services or southwest pool annex. Interiors/1875hotel are excluded.

review.method: Reuse exact cleared Qualla1911whole-exterior original first; pair with already cleared primary Highsmith entrance and native map controls.
review.notes: Two exact cleared originals cover the fixed surviving1909hotel together: the published Qualla1911PalaceHotelCompany advertisement supplies the whole eight-storey corner block, repeated window hierarchy, rounded corners and strong upper cornice; the exact Highsmith2012entrance original supplies contemporary curved door/transom/portal treatment under explicit photographer public-domain dedication. Current model retains those identifying relationships plus its native mapped full-block/lightwell/court/annex envelope. Roof service boxes, modern roof sign and attached southwest pool annex are conservative map-led exterior approximations; the1911photo does not certify those additions. Fine cornice sculpture, concealed roof joins and exact current restoration remain simplified. Original map/ground/placement and all portal geometry remain unchanged. Full fixed exterior accepted at approximate medium-fi scope; no1875reconstruction or navigable interior.

Photograph of King Kalakaua aboard USS Charleston (C-2).  The cruiser was conveying His Majesty from Honolulu to San Francisco where the King intended seeking health. The vessel reached the Golden Gate December 4. With the King were the officers of the warship including Rear-Admiral George Brown and Captain George C. Remey. His aides Major Robert Hoapili Baker and Colonel George W. Macfarlane stand directly behind the King.
